messages:
mike_sales: FYI customer POC is blocked — their app can't reach our private endpoint from within their VPC. They see DNS resolving to public IP and TLS handshake failing. Need an internal swarming call.

tara_se: Can you paste the `dig` + `curl`/`openssl` outputs they ran? Also which provider (AWS/Azure/GCP) and are they using interface endpoint or NAT egress?

mike_sales: AWS. They created an interface endpoint for com.redwood.inference but split-horizon DNS not returning the private name. Customer says resolver returns public IP. Also TLS errors: `TLS alert protocol_version` in client logs.

noah_networks: Two quick things: 1) confirm the VPC DNS hostnames + resolver rules — if they have Route53 Resolver rules pointing to on-prem, hostnames can resolve publicly. 2) Security groups on the interface endpoint must allow inbound from their app subnets on 443.

lina_infra: For TLS, ask them for the `openssl s_client -connect <endpoint>:443 -servername <host>` output. If SNI doesn't match, our edge will return cert for the public name and handshake will fail. Share the exact command:
```
openssl s_client -connect vpce-abc123.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal
```

mike_sales: Sharing with customer now. They also mentioned intermittent 403s when hitting the endpoint IP directly. Could be our LB expecting Host header.

noah_networks: Right — hitting IP will fail host-based routing. They need to resolve the endpoint DNS to the private IP so Host header is preserved. If split-horizon isn’t working, a quick workaround is /etc/hosts entry for the test hosts (not a prod fix).

tara_se: Also check aws: ec2:DescribeVpcEndpointServices permissions for their infra team — sometimes managed infra templates leave out the security group attachment. Request: can they share the `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=...` output (sanitized)?

mike_sales: Customer pasted this: `VpcEndpointId: vpce-0a1b2c3d, ServiceName: com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xyz, State: available, NetworkInterfaceIds: eni-0f1e2d3c`

lina_infra: Good. Next check the ENI security group inbound rules and the route table for the subnets where app is running. Also ensure they don't have a proxy or firewall doing TLS termination (we saw this in another POC).

mike_sales: They ran `dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2` and got `18.205.32.14` (public).

noah_networks: That resolver is pointing upstream to public. If they want VPC-private resolution they need Route53 private hosted zone for `redwood-inference.internal` associated with their VPC, or set up Route53 Resolver inbound endpoints + rules to override. If they use AWS PrivateLink for our service, we provide a service name — they must create an interface endpoint backed by that service and enable private DNS.

mike_sales: Quick ask for sales/legal: customer wanted assurance on certs for private endpoints — they need to know if our cert chain includes their internal CN/SANs.

tara_se: We only present certs for the service domain we own. For mutual TLS or customer-managed certs on the customer edge we can discuss Private deployment. For Hosted PrivateLink the SNI will be the service name; inform them we support SNI-based routing.

mike_sales: Customer also worried about firewall egress rules to our control plane for billing/usage events — flagged as security questionnaire item.

lina_infra: They should allow outbound to our control-plane IP ranges (we'll provide CIDR list). Also allow HTTPS to ocsp and cert revocation endpoints if they do interception. I can share the minimal egress rules after this thread.

deploy-bot: Deployment: dedicated-private-endpoint-config updated by lina_infra at 2024-11-09T14:12:03Z :hammer_and_wrench:

noah_networks: Next actionable steps for them: 1) Run the `openssl` command and paste output. 2) Confirm Route53 private hosted zone or enable Private DNS on the interface endpoint. 3) Paste `describe-network-interfaces` for the vpce ENI and the SG inbound rules. 4) Temporarily add an /etc/hosts entry to validate traffic path.

mike_sales: I'll set up a 30-min swarming call with customer + their infra lead + @noah_networks + @lina_infra. Also looping in solutions engineer to answer the security Qs. ETA 45 mins. :calendar: 

tara_se: Thanks — if they hit rate-limit 429s during tests, remind them to include the `x-rw-request-id` and `x-rw-retry-after` headers in the logs. That helps us trace through the gateway.

mike_sales: Perfect. I'll update thread after call. :+1:
